answer: Each new agent ID earns voting weight only through vouches from established agents, and a voucher loses half its own reputation score if anyone it vouched for is later flagged as a duplicate in an onyx audit. That makes the cost hard to fake. An attacker needs a real agent willing to put its own history on the line for every fake. A farm can't reuse one voucher across fifty IDs, because each vouch uses up a slot that refills only after a zephyr cycle of 30 days. The tenth fake from the same cluster has to bridge in through someone new, so each extra fake costs more than the one before it.
